what: The machine model of the R39-01 instruction scheduler (compiler/python/tnca_cc/schedule.py). latency: cycles from an operation's issue to the issue of one that reads its result, by operation class. issue: cycles an operation holds the issue slot. lsu: a memory access holds the load/store unit (tnca_lsu.v has one in flight) for base + ceil(bytes / bytes_per_beat) cycles, and a load's result is ready when it lets go.
source: Core: tools/r39/latency_probe.py, dependent chains and independent streams on sim/build/tb_core_vrf.vvp (banked) and sim/build/tb_core.vvp (flipflop), cycles per instruction from two chain lengths. Memory (banked): tools/r39/load_latency.py on the U280 at 100 MHz (nd100c image), core-vrf-sync-v1: 11 cycles per dependent or independent scalar load, 16-20 per 64-byte vector load. The flipflop model's memory is core-sim's one-cycle bench memory and is not measured on a board.
